title: saber, sí / si, long sentences, explicar

cards.title: saber = to know
cards.body: Link it to British slang 'savvy', which comes from the same Latin root. Note the b in saber sounds close to the v in savvy.

examples.en: I want to know why he doesn't want to know.
examples.es: Quiero saber por qué no quiere saber.

cards.title: sí = yes, si = if
cards.body: Same sound: with an accent (sí) it means yes, without (si) it means if.

examples.en: I want to know if you (formal) want to know.
I want to know if he wants to invite me.
I don't want to imagine it.

cards.title: The a stays with venir
cards.body: Even with a la casa in between, venir still connects to the next verb with a.

examples.en: I want to know if she wants to come to the house to visit me.
examples.es: Quiero saber si quiere venir a la casa a visitarme.

examples.en: … why she doesn't want to come …
examples.es: Quiero saber por qué no quiere venir a la casa a visitarme.

cards.title: Try what you think you can't say
cards.body: English gives you a lot of vocabulary that converts to Spanish; you only discover it by trying.

cards.title: Listening: work out the meaning
cards.body: When listening, lo could be him, it or formal you; pick the meaning that fits. Translate into natural English: '¿Por qué no quiere informarme?' can be 'Why doesn't he want to let me know?'.

examples.en: I'm going to invite him, but I'm not going to invite him now.
examples.es: Voy a invitarlo, pero no voy a invitarlo ahora.

examples.en: I want to start it now.

cards.title: justificar — throaty j
cards.body: Justification has the English 'j' sound, so it becomes the throaty sound.

examples.en: I'm not trying to justify myself.

cards.title: explicar — an exception
cards.body: Explanation is explicación, not 'explanación' (compare English inexplicable). So 'to explain' is explicar. Spanish can say 'explain you something'.

examples.en: But I want to explain something to you.

cards.title: Focus on one block at a time
cards.body: Put all your attention on the current block, say it, then let it go and move to the next.

examples.en: I'm not trying to justify myself, but I want to explain something to you.
examples.es: No intento justificarme, pero quiero explicarte algo.

practice.en: I want to know why he doesn't want to know.
es: Quiero saber por qué no quiere saber
Quiero saber porque no quiere saber
practice.why: quiero saber + por qué + no quiere saber.
sí with an accent = yes; si = if.

practice.en: I want to know if he wants to invite me.
I don't want to imagine it.
I want to know if she wants to come to the house to visit me.
es: Quiero saber si quiere venir a la casa a visitarme
practice.why: Keep the a after venir: a la casa a visitarme.

practice.en: I'm not trying to justify myself.
But I want to explain something to you.
I want to start it now.
I'm going to invite him, but not now.
es: Voy a invitarlo pero no ahora
practice.why: voy a invitarlo + pero no ahora.
